Youth Unemployment - Empty promises

By: Mart-Marie Faure | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Unemployment has been declared a national crisis but does government really have a plan or is it just a case of more empty promises.

Unique Selling Point:
Thousands of young South Africans enter the job market filled with hope. Many will be bitterly disappointed. Almost 8 million of the country's young people under the age of 34 will not be employed nor will they be enrolled in any from of education or training leaving them destitute with no hope for the future. Sixty percent of those who enter the employment market without a matric are jobless and many of these young people now believe that there's no hope that they will ever find a job.Youth aged 15-24 are the most vulnerable group in the labour market.
There existence is eked out on a day-to day basis. We will tell the story of 3 unemployed youths and the daily challenges that they face.



Summary:
Government's responses to youth unemployment have almost failed to recognize the scale of the challenge.Politicians have mentioned the youth time and time again in their speeches but so far government has been unable to come up with a workable plan. No Project or initiative will have a significant impact on overall outcomes. last year Pres. Ramaposha introduced the highly criticized Youth Employment Strategy. The President aims to set the country on a new path of growth and employment,
but once again the process of job creation was politicized. The Yes programme is now linked to the BEE scorecard and promises enterprises that wish to claim this benefit need to get measured on the full scorecard before they can benefit from Yes.The process is costly and complicated4 go through a verification to get to a level The question asked is why would an exempt micro enterprise that is automatically level 4 go through the verification. Similarly , why would a 51% black-owned QSE want to get verified? This leaves businesses without any realy initiative to become part of the initiative. So what is the solution? Should job creation be left in the hands of the government or are there other alternatives. Yes, there are says GG Alcock. Recognising the informal sector as an integral part of the economy and job creation is a crucial first step.
We will explore this as part of the story.

Unique Selling Point: Thousands of young South Africans enter the job market filled with hope. Many will be bitterly disappointed. Almost 8 million of the country's young people under the age of 34 will not be employed nor will they be enrolled in any from of education or training leaving them destitute with no hope for the future. Sixty percent of those who enter the employment market without a matric are jobless and many of these young people now believe that there's no hope that they will ever find a job.Youth aged 15-24 are the most vulnerable group in the labour market. There existence is eked out on a day-to day basis. We will tell the story of 3 unemployed youths and the daily challenges that they face. Summary: Government's responses to youth unemployment have almost failed to recognize the scale of the challenge.Politicians have mentioned the youth time and time again in their speeches but so far government has been unable to come up with a workable plan. No Project or initiative will have a significant impact on overall outcomes. last year Pres. Ramaposha introduced the highly criticized Youth Employment Strategy. The President aims to set the country on a new path of growth and employment, but once again the process of job creation was politicized. The Yes programme is now linked to the BEE scorecard and promises enterprises that wish to claim this benefit need to get measured on the full scorecard before they can benefit from Yes.The process is costly and complicated4 go through a verification to get to a level The question asked is why would an exempt micro enterprise that is automatically level 4 go through the verification. Similarly , why would a 51% black-owned QSE want to get verified? This leaves businesses without any realy initiative to become part of the initiative. So what is the solution? Should job creation be left in the hands of the government or are there other alternatives. Yes, there are says GG Alcock. Recognising the informal sector as an integral part of the economy and job creation is a crucial first step. We will explore this as part of the story. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Unemployment has been declared a national crisis but does government really have a plan or is it just a case of more empty promises.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Thousands of young South Africans enter the job market filled with hope. Many will be bitterly disappointed. Almost 8 million of the country's young people under the age of 34 will not be employed nor will they be enrolled in any from of education or training leaving them destitute with no hope for the future. Sixty percent of those who enter the employment market without a matric are jobless and many of these young people now believe that there's no hope that they will ever find a job.Youth aged 15-24 are the most vulnerable group in the labour market. There existence is eked out on a day-to day basis. We will tell the story of 3 unemployed youths and the daily challenges that they face.
metadata.Summary: Government's responses to youth unemployment have almost failed to recognize the scale of the challenge.Politicians have mentioned the youth time and time again in their speeches but so far government has been unable to come up with a workable plan. No Project or initiative will have a significant impact on overall outcomes. last year Pres. Ramaposha introduced the highly criticized Youth Employment Strategy. The President aims to set the country on a new path of growth and employment, but once again the process of job creation was politicized. The Yes programme is now linked to the BEE scorecard and promises enterprises that wish to claim this benefit need to get measured on the full scorecard before they can benefit from Yes.The process is costly and complicated4 go through a verification to get to a level The question asked is why would an exempt micro enterprise that is automatically level 4 go through the verification. Similarly , why would a 51% black-owned QSE want to get verified? This leaves businesses without any realy initiative to become part of the initiative. So what is the solution? Should job creation be left in the hands of the government or are there other alternatives. Yes, there are says GG Alcock. Recognising the informal sector as an integral part of the economy and job creation is a crucial first step. We will explore this as part of the story.
